To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the age‐related decline in Nrf2 binding at an ARE locus in the GclC gene promoter is associated with an age‐specific shift in Nrf2 DNA‐binding activity from an active to an alternate ARE site.
age‐related loss in Nrf2‐ARE binding to the Gclc promoter is due, in part, to a compensatory switch from a functional ARE to a nonfunctional ARE site.

the age‐related decrease in hepatic glutathione synthetic enzyme capacity is due to the loss of Nrf2 DNA‐binding activity to the active ARE site in the Gclc gene, which leads to the compensatory binding to a second ARE element.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the age‐related decline in the ability to detoxify harmful chemicals.
the identification of an age‐related change in the Nrf2‐ARE binding site that may explain why the expression of the GCLC gene, a key enzyme in glutathione synthetic, is diminished during aging.
how aging alters the ability of the liver to maintain its antioxidant defenses and how this is accomplished by Nrf2‐ARE signaling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Nrf2‐dependent gene expression is altered with age and that this is due in part to a loss of Nrf2 DNA‐binding activity, which is compensated for in part by the occupation of alternative ARE elements.
Nrf2‐ARE DNA binding and gene expression is altered in aging and that this may contribute to a diminished ability to detoxify electrophiles and reactive oxygen species.
the loss of Nrf2‐dependent GCLC gene expression in aging liver is due to a combination of age‐specific changes in Nrf2 DNA‐binding and the presence of transcriptional repressor proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

aging results in the loss of basal Gclc gene expression because Nrf2 is not able to bind to the active ARE of the Gclc gene, which is compensated by the occupation of an alternative, but less effective, ARE site.
the aging process leads to a decline in Nrf2‐ARE binding and a compensatory shift in binding to another ARE site in the promoter of Gclc.

the aging process is accompanied by a loss in the ability to activate the Nrf2/ARE signaling pathway, and that the loss of Nrf2‐ARE binding is a compensatory means to maintain basal expression in the aged liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Nrf2‐regulated gene expression is modulated by age‐specific changes in Nrf2 binding and transcriptional coregulators, and that the age‐specific loss of glutathone synthetic capacity is not solely due to a loss of Nrf2 nuclear levels.
age‐specific changes to Nrf2‐ARE binding can occur and may be an important factor in modulating gene expression during the aging process.
the aging process alters Nrf2 binding and that this change in Nrf2 DNA occupancy is a compensatory response to the age‐associated decline in phase II detoxification.
